docs.title: Product Vault overview
docs.text: The Product Vault (the Vault) maintains your product assets: forms, rules, rates and supporting documents. It is the single source of truth for your products. Product, actuarial, compliance and filing teams all work from the same current version, so nobody has to hunt for the right file.

docs.title: What the Vault holds
docs.text:
Asset Where you find it Forms Forms tab Manuals (rates and rules) Manuals tab Rules Rules tab, pulled from your manuals Supporting documents Supporting Materials tab

Assets are organized by product and by jurisdiction (a state the product is available in). You upload, process and publish one jurisdiction at a time.

docs.title: How the Vault fits the lifecycle
docs.text:
1. The product's assets live in the Vault.
  2. The team opens a project in the Project Workbench to create or change a product.
  3. Actuaries test scenarios and settle rates and rules in the Rating Sandbox.
  4. Filing Manager carries the product through filing and approval.
  5. The Rating Catalog supplies the rater and services such as the clause library.
  6. Every finished change returns to the Vault, so it stays current.

docs.title: The Vault journey
docs.text:
Step Page Product status 1. Get your tenant and lists ready Before you start 2. Create the product with its states Create a product 3. Upload documents for each state Import documents Pending Import 4. Add metadata and process Process documents Processing → Processed 5. Publish the jurisdiction Review and publish Published (Baseline)

Once a jurisdiction is published, your team can start a Product Update in the Workbench.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: A few one-time setup steps make creating products in the Vault smooth.

docs.title: Sign in and choose your tenant
docs.text:
1. Sign in with your email first, then your password.
  2. Open the user menu (your initials) and confirm the organization shown, for example Organization — {tenant}.
  3. To change tenant, choose Switch Tenant and select the tenant you want, then Confirm.

Use a test tenant for practice

Try new steps in a test tenant first. Administrators viewing another tenant see a yellow banner with Switch Back.

docs.title: Set up Group and Underwriting Company
docs.text:
Every product needs a Group and an Underwriting Company. Underwriting Company depends on Group, so each company must sit under a group.

  1. Go to System Administration → Lists.
  2. Create the Group value first.
  3. Open Underwriting Company and choose the Grouped by Group view.
  4. Select + Add value under {Group} and enter the company name.
  5. Reload the page and reopen Underwriting Company. The companies should still appear under the group.

Note

If the Underwriting Company field later shows No Options when you create a product, the companies are not linked to a group yet. Repeat the steps above.

docs.title: Check your product list
docs.text: Products are created from your tenant's product list (lines such as Personal and Commercial, and products such as Auto or Homeowners). Make sure the products you need are on the list before you create them. TODO verify where the product list is managed.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Open Product Vault from the left navigation.
  2. Choose Add Existing Product. You can also start from Import Product on the Dashboard. TODO verify button labels.
  3. Choose the line and product, for example Personal → Auto.
  4. Enter the product name.
  5. Select the Group and a linked Underwriting Company.
  6. Select every state (jurisdiction) the product needs.
  7. Save the product, then open it and confirm the states appear.

Choose states carefully

Add all states when you create the product and double-check them before you save (for example AK, not AZ). A way to add a state to an existing product has not been documented yet. TODO verify

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Line Product States Personal Auto AK, AL Personal Homeowners AK, AL Commercial Motor Truck Cargo AK, AL

Next: Import documents.

docs.title: Import documents
docs.text: You upload documents for one jurisdiction at a time. There is no product-level upload.

docs.title: Prepare your files
docs.text:
A simple folder layout keeps imports fast:

{Product}/{State}/Forms/                 .doc or .docx files
{Product}/{State}/Manuals/
{Product}/{State}/Supporting Documents/  goes to the Supporting Materials tab

docs.title: Upload for a state
docs.text:
1. Open the product in the Product Vault and select the jurisdiction.
  2. Open the upload or import view for that jurisdiction. TODO verify button label.
  3. On Forms, use Bulk Import and choose the folder of .doc or .docx forms for that state.
  4. On Manuals, upload the manuals for that state.
  5. On Supporting Materials, upload the supporting documents for that state.
  6. Let each upload finish before you move to the next tab or state.

Suggested order: finish one state completely (Forms → Manuals → Supporting Materials), then move to the next.

docs.title: Check the counts
docs.text:
An upload is complete when the counts in each tab match your files. For example:

Product State Forms Manuals Supporting Materials Auto AK 2 4 2 Auto AL 2 4 2 Homeowners AK 2 5 2 Homeowners AL 2 5 2

After upload the jurisdiction shows Pending Import. That is expected: the next step is Process documents.

docs.title: Process documents
docs.text: Processing turns uploaded files into Vault assets. It needs a little metadata first.

docs.title: 1. Add form metadata
docs.text:
1. Open the jurisdiction → Forms.
  2. Open a row's metadata dialog.
  3. Enter Form Number and Edition. These are the only required fields.
  4. Close the dialog. Closing saves your changes.

Form file names usually follow {PREFIX} {NNNN} {MM} {YY} {Title}.docx:

File name starts with Form Number Edition PPA 0001 07 16 PPA 0001 07 16 HO 0003 09 20 HO 0003 09 20

docs.title: 2. Add manual editions
docs.text:
1. Open Manuals.
  2. For each row, select Edit, enter the Edition, then Save Metadata.
File name clue Edition 01 21, Rev 06 21 01 21, 06 21 Four digits at the end, such as 0823 08 23

docs.title: 3. Process
docs.text:
1. Select Process Documents once.
  2. The status moves to Processing, then Processed. This can take a minute or two. Refresh the page to see the update.
  3. When processing is done, you see Rater and Review & Publish.

Tip

Select Process Documents only once and give it time to finish.

Next: Review and publish.

docs.title: Review and publish
docs.text: Publishing makes a processed jurisdiction the current baseline in the Vault. Your team needs a published product before they can update it in the Project Workbench.

docs.title: 1. Check rules
docs.text: Rules are pulled from your manuals. Open Rules and expand the tree, for example 1 MANUAL FORMAT → 1.1 Multistate Rules Manual. Make sure numbering is complete. If something is missing, check the manual editions on the Manuals tab.

docs.title: 2. Publish
docs.text:
1. Select Review & Publish.
  2. Review the counts. Information Pending should be 0 for Manuals, Forms and Supporting Materials.
  3. Choose the Type of Insurance, for example 19.0 Personal Auto.
  4. Check each Subtype of Insurance that applies.
  5. Set the Effective Date.
  6. Select Publish.
  7. Confirm the release shows as Baseline under Product Resources. TODO verify exact label.

Repeat for each jurisdiction you want to publish.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text: Start a Product Update in the Workbench: Workbench → + New Project → Product Update. TODO verify once the Workbench pages are written.
